title: Ponerse, Volverse, Hacerse: How to Say “Become” in Spanish
seo_title: Ponerse, Volverse, Hacerse: How to Say “Become” in Spanish
meta_description: Ponerse, volverse, hacerse, quedarse and convertirse: how to say become in Spanish. When each verb fits, clear examples, common mistakes and a quick quiz.
excerpt: Spanish has five ways to say “become”. Here’s which one to use, and why.

body_html:
Ponerse, volverse, hacerse: English has one easy verb, “to become” (or “to get”), but Spanish has several, and each describes a different kind of change. A sudden blush, a slow change of character, a career reached through effort and a change caused by circumstances all use different verbs. It sounds complicated, but there is a clear logic, and a few examples make it stick.

Quick answer
  • Ponerse + adjective: sudden or temporary changes (mood, appearance). Se puso rojo.
  • Volverse + adjective: deep, lasting change, often involuntary. Se volvió muy serio.
  • Hacerse + noun/adjective: change through effort or gradual process. Se hizo médico.
  • Quedarse: change as a result of an event. Se quedó sin trabajo. Convertirse en + noun: transformation.
{{toc}}

Ponerse, volverse, hacerse at a glance

VerbKind of changeExample
ponerseSudden, temporary: emotions, color, healthMe puse nervioso. I got nervous.
volverseDeep, lasting, often unexpectedSe ha vuelto muy egoísta. He’s become very selfish.
hacerseThrough effort, choice or timeSe hizo rica. She became rich.
quedarseResult of an event or lossSe quedó ciego. He went blind.
convertirse enTransformation into something elseEl pueblo se convirtió en una ciudad.
llegar a serAchievement after a long processLlegó a ser directora. She became director.

Ponerse: sudden, temporary changes

Use ponerse with adjectives for changes in mood, color or physical state that happen quickly and usually don’t last.

  • Se puso rojo cuando lo vio. He blushed when he saw her.
  • Me pongo nerviosa antes de un examen. I get nervous before an exam.
  • Mi madre se puso muy contenta. My mother got very happy.
  • El niño se puso enfermo. The child got sick.

The RAE dictionary lists this use of ponerse: to acquire a particular state or condition. It pairs naturally with emotion words; see {{link:talking-about-feelings-in-spanish|talking about feelings in Spanish}}.

Volverse: deep, lasting change

Volverse describes a change in someone’s character or nature, often gradual and not chosen. It frequently sounds dramatic or negative.

  • Se volvió loco. He went mad.
  • Desde que es famosa, se ha vuelto muy arrogante. Since she became famous, she’s become very arrogant.
  • El tema se volvió muy complicado. The issue became very complicated.
{{image:2}}

Hacerse: change through effort or time

Hacerse suggests a change that comes from effort, choice or a natural process. It is common with professions, wealth and age.

  • Se hizo abogado. He became a lawyer.
  • Se hicieron amigos en la universidad. They became friends at university.
  • Se está haciendo tarde. It’s getting late.
  • Me estoy haciendo mayor. I’m getting older.
{{book:the-mind-lies}}

Quedarse: change as a result

Quedarse describes the state you end up in after something happens, often a loss:

  • Se quedó sin trabajo. He lost his job (was left without work).
  • Mi abuelo se quedó sordo. My grandfather went deaf.
  • Me quedé sorprendido. I was surprised.

See {{link:quedar-vs-quedarse|quedar vs quedarse}} for more uses.

Convertirse en and llegar a ser

Convertirse en + noun is a transformation: La oruga se convirtió en mariposa (The caterpillar turned into a butterfly). Llegar a ser emphasizes achievement after a long road: Llegó a ser campeón del mundo (He went on to become world champion).

Real conversations

  • A: ¿Qué tal la entrevista? (How was the interview?)
  • B: Al principio me puse muy nervioso, pero luego me relajé. (At first I got very nervous, but then I relaxed.)
  • A: ¡Seguro que te dan el puesto y te haces jefe! (I’m sure you’ll get the job and become the boss!)
  • B: Jaja, ojalá. Mientras no me vuelva un jefe insoportable… (Haha, I hope so. As long as I don’t turn into an unbearable boss…)

Common mistakes

IncorrectCorrectWhy
Me volví nervioso antes del examen.Me puse nervioso antes del examen.Temporary emotion: ponerse
Se puso médico.Se hizo médico.Profession through effort: hacerse
Llegó a ser rojo.Se puso rojo.Sudden color change
Se convirtió famoso.Se hizo famoso.Convertirse en needs a noun

Try it yourself

  1. She got angry when she heard the news. (Se puso furiosa cuando oyó la noticia.)
  2. They became famous overnight. (Se hicieron famosos de la noche a la mañana.)
  3. He’s become very quiet lately. (Se ha vuelto muy callado últimamente.)
  4. The house turned into a museum. (La casa se convirtió en un museo.)
  5. I ran out of money. (Me quedé sin dinero.)

A quick way to practice: describe one change in your own life with each verb, for example how you feel before a test, a friend who has changed, and a goal you reached. For more verb pairs that learners mix up, see {{link:spanish-confusing-words|my complete list of Spanish confusing words}}.

{{quiz}}

Final thoughts

To say “become” in Spanish, ask what kind of change it is. Sudden mood or color: ponerse. Deep change in character: volverse. Effort or time: hacerse. Result of an event: quedarse. Transformation into something new: convertirse en. Once you ask that question, the verb chooses itself.

faq.q: How do you say “to become” in Spanish?
faq.a: It depends on the change: ponerse for sudden, temporary states, volverse for deep changes in character, hacerse for change through effort, quedarse for results of an event and convertirse en for transformations.

faq.q: Is it ponerse or volverse nervioso?
faq.a: Ponerse nervioso, because nervousness is a sudden, temporary state.

faq.q: How do you say “she became a doctor” in Spanish?
faq.a: Se hizo médica, or llegó a ser médica to emphasize the long effort.

questions.explain: A profession reached through effort: hacerse.

questions.q: Con los años ___ muy desconfiado. (He became very distrustful.)
questions.explain: A lasting change in character: volverse.
The result of an event: quedarse.

questions.q: El pequeño pueblo ___ una gran ciudad.
questions.explain: Transformation into something new (noun): convertirse en.
